summary.text: 车 is the modern simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a wheeled vehicle. Its present shape derives from the cursive form of 車.

formation.text: The traditional graph 車 is a whole-graph pictograph: early forms depict varying features of a vehicle, such as wheels, a body or frame, and axle or pole elements. Those forms were reduced and regularized over time. The current graph 车 is a later cursive-derived simplified form of 車.

components.text: 车 is the modern simplified form derived from cursive 車. It represents the complete vehicle pictograph, not a separate part of it.

history.text: Early oracle-bone and bronze forms of 車 varied in the vehicle features they showed. Later forms selected and regularized some features. The curated oracle-bone, Western Zhou bronze, and seal-script examples illustrate distinct presentations; they are modern redrawings, not artifact photographs.
The simplified form 车 derives from cursive 車, attested by the Sui dynasty at the latest. It became a standard character in 1956, a change distinct from the earlier variation and reduction of 車.

uncertainties.text: Early forms varied, and the curated images are modern redrawings; descriptions of individual vehicle features in any one image should therefore be treated cautiously.
Early vehicle uses are identified by inscription references, but the cited evidence gives no calendar dates for those inscriptions or a precise earliest date for the graph.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 車 for vehicles, while bronze examples include vehicles and war chariots. These attest early vehicle-related use, but not a calendar-dated first occurrence.
An oracle-bone example is identified as a place-name use. Its meaning and any historical connection to the vehicle sense are unresolved.

senses.gloss: wheeled machines; transporting by cart; cartload measure
senses.text: Later dictionaries record these uses, but the evidence does not date their emergence or establish a continuous development from the vehicle sense.
The common modern meaning includes vehicle and car.

limitations.text: The chronology and semantic links among later machinery, transport, and measure senses are unresolved, so no chain of development is proposed.

Some proposals suggest the spoken word written 車 was borrowed from Indo-Iranian words for “wheel” or “chariot.” In that account, the graph was reused for a different word because the words sounded alike or similar; the vehicle picture did not develop into a new meaning. The depicted vehicle’s spoken name is not independently established, so the proposed sound match remains disputed.
The traditional account that Xi Zhong made the vehicle in the Xia period is not independently confirmed by the cited evidence.

overview.text: 车 is the simplified form of 車, whose early forms pictured a wheeled vehicle. The modern shape comes from cursive writing of the traditional character.

components.text: This is the simplified form of the whole vehicle picture, derived from cursive 車; it is not a separate part of that picture.

relationships.text: 车 is the modern simplified form derived from cursive 車.
